_read: Fleet-level expectation cases, read from the book. The unit-level cases are in golden_cases.json; this file answers another question: what the FLEET's legality checks must say when a fleet is assembled around a sentence of the book. The driver is the same test_golden.js.
_why_own_file: golden_cases.json is 4600 lines of unit cases and it is edited in parallel in another session (the card cases). The fleet cases have a different shape and a different run, so they are in their own file. 1.1 phase 1, 14.9.2026.
_shape: { id, page, the list name in fleet.list, fleet: { list, limit, units: [ { entry (a regex for the list row) | ship (page number), n (hulls, default 1), repeat (how many SEPARATE units, default 1), opts: [{option, state, qty}], ups: [{upgrade, state}], adjust, list (source list, only in phase 3) } ] }, expect: { total, checks: [{ src | label, ok, v, warn, absent }], facts: [{ src | label, v, warn, absent }] (J214: fleet facts, attack rating etc.), others_ok, failing }, why }
_checks: src = the book's sentence as it is in the rule's src field (a substring, normalised); label = a regex of the check row's heading. Each may hit exactly one row. others_ok = no other row may be red. failing = the exact number of red rows.
